title: Stanley Prusiner (1942–) — The Unkillable Brain Rot, Coining 'Prion,' Tenure Denied, and the 1997 Unshared Nobel

teenKit.tldr: A young neurologist named Stanley Prusiner risked his entire career by proving that a fatal brain disease was caused by a protein with zero genetic material—violating every rule of biology.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This breakthrough forced science to accept that biological information can be transmitted by corrupted shapes alone, opening doors to understanding modern neurodegenerative nightmares like Alzheimer's.
keyTakeaways: Prusiner targeted an abandoned, high-pain medical mystery (scrapie/CJD) that mainstream scientists avoided because it defied standard viral or bacterial models.
He bypassed traditional institutional gatekeepers and funding blockades by leveraging private philanthropy to sustain his brutal 25-year investigation.
By stacking irreversible physical proofs and coining a brand-new term, he permanently altered how we define infectious agents.

quiz.question: What made the 60-year-old patient's decline on the Moffatt ward so historically shocking to medicine?
options: It was caused by a common bacterial infection easily treated with antibiotics.
It took forty agonizing years to slowly progress into mild forgetfulness.
It completely destroyed her mind and body in a terrifying 60-day biological freefall.

quiz.explanation: The sheer velocity of the collapse—from a sharp, active adult to death in just two months with no logical explanation—shattered standard medical assumptions.
